item.meridian_basic_techniques.later_bre: Canon of Tracing Breath - Gathering Chapter
technique.meridian_basic_techniques.late: This art consumes qi while maintained, even when you are not breathing. When you breathe, it gathers more qi with less effort.
codex.intro.meridian_basic_techniques.la: Later cultivators gradually developed this breathing art. Its method of guiding qi returned with your memories of a former life, and even reborn in youth, you still remember how to practice it.
codex.power.meridian_basic_techniques.la: Follow this art to gather more qi through breathing, with less strain.
technique.meridian_basic_techniques.brea: arms and legs recover four times faster for 20 s; heals no wounds, restores no qi
technique.meridian_basic_techniques.ligh: for 20 s a jump becomes a leap toward the crosshair, up to 7 blocks; sneaking jumps normally
technique.meridian_basic_techniques.char: arm strength up by three tenths for a few seconds, then a spell of weakness
technique.meridian_basic_techniques.guar: Hold to raise both forearms over head and torso; blows and arrows from the front land on a forearm, three tenths lighter. With a sword or an axe in the main hand you parry with the weapon instead; it takes most of the force and wears down, and it shatters when its durability runs out. Release to lower
advancements.meridian_basic_techniques.c: Catch your breath to shake off weariness, tuck the waist to vault cliffs, and sink the breath low to swing with crushing weight—the three crude rudiments, fully mastered.
codex.intro.meridian_basic_techniques.ba: A porter catching his breath, a hunter watching mountain goats leap crags, a smith sinking his weight into the anvil—the bare foundation of breath and brace for wandering the realm.
codex.power.meridian_basic_techniques.br: Halt your stride, open the chest, and draw in breath. After hard miles on the road, exhaling the stale air clears the ache from weary limbs in no time.
codex.power.meridian_basic_techniques.li: Borrowed from crag goats on sheer cliffs: a light tap off the stone, a tuck of the waist, and you spring clean over a ledge taller than a man.
codex.power.meridian_basic_techniques.ch: Learned from smiths raising heavy hammers: sink the shoulders, pack your breath deep in the gut, and the blow lands with brutal, unyielding weight.
